scope_note: All thirteen preserved HTML records were read in full, including headers, bodies, excluded annotations, XML constraints, summaries, footnotes, bibliographies and scholarly sections. Every explicit upper bound is 1857-1868, outside 1844-1846. The later Huxley reply and Darwin reply form distinctive 1857 exchange evidence but cannot be back-projected.

record_reviews.source_kind: preserved HTML letter with annotations, footnotes, bibliography and scholarly section
record_reviews.summary: Huxley answers Darwin's genealogical classification view: morphology and development must precede scientific zoology, while pedigree belongs to physiology. This is a distinctive reply to the cited 26 September 1857 Darwin letter.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML bounded_range 1809-01-01–1857-10-02; [before 3 October 1857], dated by the 3 October 1857 relationship. No 1844-1846 constraint.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: T. H. Huxley authored surviving incoming body; CD notes and editorial scholarly section remain separate.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Distinctive later reply; antecedent is cited editorially but not present as a supported packet edge.

evidence.quote: Your pedigree business is a part of Physiology
